newsitem.title: FRANCE: French interior minister's ratings soar after raid.
newsitem.headline: French interior minister's ratings soar after raid.

text.p: French Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre's popularity soared after he ordered police to raid a Paris church and evict African immigrants seeking legal residence, an opinion poll found on Thursday.

Debre's rating jumped nine percentage points in a month's time, to 32 percent, when voters were asked whether they would like him to play an important role in politics in the future, according to the SOFRES poll for the weekly Le Figaro magazine.
By contrast, voters saw the fortunes of conservative President Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Alain Juppe dipping slightly compared to the previous month.
According to the poll, 40 percent had confidence in Chirac compared to 43 percent in August while just 34 percent had confidence in Juppe, down from 36 percent a month earlier.
The two French leaders have been plagued by near-record unemployment, a stagnating economy and threats of labour unrest over government austerity plans.
Three in four French adults said battling unemployment should be the government's top priority, according to the poll, conducted last Wednesday through Friday.
Immigration has been a hot issue in France since some 300 Africans occupied a Paris church in late June in a protest aimed at France's tough immigration laws.

After initially ignoring the protesters, the government announced it would be illegal to allow them to remain in France and mounted a high-profile dawn raid on the church while promising a humanitarian case-by-case review of their situation.
